sentences.text:
This appeal is filed under Section 54(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 challenging the judgment and award dated 17.04.2021 passed by the VII Additional District Judge, Tumakuru in R.A.
No.73/2020 by which the appeal filed for enhancement of market value was dismissed on the ground that the petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act was filed after the limitation period.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants submits that in the appeal filed by the claimant, the learned District Judge was not justified in dismissing the appeal on the ground that the petition Mahadevamma vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104717529/

sentences.text: 3. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1-State submits that, there was an inordinate delay in filing the appeal under Section 54(1) of the Act and hence, the learned District Judge has rightly passed the impugned judgment and the same does not warrant any interference.
4. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties.
5. The appellant/claimant being dissatisfied with the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, had filed a petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The Reference Court allowed the petition in part, and awarded compensation of Rs.10,500/- for 7 guntas of acquired land and fixed the market value at Rs.48,000/-, towards four Mango trees, and Rs.22,684/- towards two Jack Fruit trees, and Rs.8,000/- towards one pongamia tree and Rs.7,450/- towards two tamarind trees.
6. The appeal was filed after an inordinate delay of 8 years.

The learned District Judge instead of considering, whether there was sufficient cause, to condone the delay in filing the appeal passed the impugned judgment, holding that the reference petition was not filed within limitation period.
In the absence of challenge to the award passed by the Reference Court, the impugned Judgment passed by the First Appellate Court is not sustainable in law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.
ii. The impugned judgment dated 17.04.2021 passed by the learned District Judge in R.A.No.73/2020 is hereby set aside and the matter is remanded to learned District judge to hear the appeal afresh and pass appropriate order in accordance with law.
iii. The appellant is entitled for admissible Court fee paid on this appeal, and the Registry to transfer the admissible Court fee to which the appellant is entitled, to the First Appellate Court to enable the appellant/claimant herein to withdraw the Court fee.
